newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates dip but gilts stay firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates dip but gilts stay firm.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 6.75-7.25 percent on Wednesday, down from the day's opening of 7.50-8.00 percent, dealers said.

The market opened at 8.0 percent and soon dropped to 6.75-7.00 percent, a dealer at Discount and Finance House of India said. She said there were stray deals at 6.50 percent, but the rates soon firmed to 7.00-7.25 percent towards the close.
"The market was quiet, with some ex-voucher trading in 13.50 percent maturing in 1998 at 100.30-35 rupees," M.Srinivas of Centurion Bank said.
A National Stock Exchange (NSE) dealer said the day's volume on the exchange was 2.31 billion rupees on Wednesday against Tuesday's trade of 1.40 billion rupees.

He said the 13.50 percent government security maturing in 1997 was traded at 12.83 percent, down from Tuesday's level of 12.95 percent, while 13.50 percent 1998 was traded at 13.31 percent against Tuesday's level of 13.36 percent.

The market also saw some trades in 13.82 percent 2002 at 13.82 percent and 13.70 percent 1999 at 13.56 percent. The zero coupon bond maturing in 1999 and 2000 were traded at 13.78 and 13.90 percent respectively, he added.

The treasury bill maturing in November 1996 was traded at 8.50-55 percent levels, the January 1997 treasury bill at 9.75 percent and the treasury bill maturing in August 1997 at 12.45 percent, dealers said.
Inter-corporate deposit rates were steady at 18-20 percent for blue-chip companies and commercial paper (CP) of Dabur India was traded at 11.5 percent for November maturity.
Certificate of deposits (CD) of financial institutions were quoted at 15.00 percent for one year maturity, a dealer said.
